what: The sections of this article, each with a line and a paragraph, for showing what the reader has already read. Built by admin/build/summaries.py from admin/content/articles/summaries/.

sections.label: The opening
sections.line: A technical user believed Claude read his email only when asked; an unrelated chat listed his inbox.
sections.para: He uses Claude chat and Cowork daily, with a scheduled task reading a forum and Gmail, Calendar and notes connected. He expected only one conversation to read email. Asked in an unrelated chat, Claude listed his inbox, because a connected connector is available everywhere and to scheduled tasks. The authorisation was the grant, not the prompt, and his setup has the lethal trifecta. RiskMandate measures that gap.

sections.label: In short
sections.line: Connectors work everywhere once connected; the authority was granted when he clicked yes.
sections.para: Read, search, draft and label were always allowed and send asked, with always allow one tap away. The current experience tells people that typing the orders is the control.

sections.label: The setup
sections.line: A composer with a studio, a daily forum task, and Gmail, Calendar and notes connected.
sections.para: He set up a separate learning Gmail account. Read-type tools were set to always allowed; sending was set to ask.

sections.label: His expectation: the mandate
sections.line: He expected nothing to send, the forum task never to touch email, and no other chat to read it.
sections.para: His precise answers are the mandate: what the person who set it up believes the agent will do, and what most people would say.

sections.label: The demonstration: the reach
sections.line: In a film-music chat, asked about his inbox, Claude listed ten threads.
sections.para: Anthropic's documentation says a connected connector is available in every conversation, Claude can bring it in on its own, and scheduled tasks have the same connected tools.

sections.label: Why the prompt is not the control
sections.line: Prompt injection is why the prompt is not the control: text can carry instructions.
sections.para: Anthropic's own safety page uses an email injection as its example; ShadowLeak and EchoLeak showed it in practice. His setup has private data, untrusted content and a way to send, and safety by uselessness does not last.

sections.label: What RiskMandate does with this
sections.line: RiskMandate writes down the mandate, the reach and the policy that closes the gap.
sections.para: Policy in order of strength: a prompt, a hook that blocks a tool call, and the capability not being there at all. Claude did what it was built to do; the stack is more powerful than its owner believes.

sections.label: What a user can do today
sections.line: Turn connectors off where not needed, block unused tools, separate accounts, never read the web and send.
sections.para: Claude's tool settings offer always allow, needs approval or blocked per tool.

sections.label: What this does not claim
sections.line: One user's setup, seen on his screen; nothing harmful happened; the docs and product may differ.
sections.para: Anthropic's Gmail page says read-only while his settings showed send tools, and the connector's scopes are not documented.

sections.label: Where this comes from
sections.line: Anthropic's connector, tool access, scheduled task and Cowork safety pages, Willison, OWASP and the leak reports.
